page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Compute resources consist of 8 physical cores providing 16 dedicated vCPUs through 2 threads per core, combined with 64.0 GB of system memory.

Resource allocation follows a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage, meaning primary persistence relies on external block storage services. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Because the configuration uses dedicated core scheduling rather than shared or burstable threads, compute capacity remains consistent under sustained load. The balanced allocation between CPU cores and memory makes the server appropriate for mid-tier application hosting, continuous integration and build nodes, web serving fleets, and general containerized workloads.

System memory is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a standard ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent data requirements. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated compute allocation and balanced resource sizing, this configuration provides predictable processing capability without shared-core contention. It is suited for mid-sized general compute tasks, including microservice hosting, enterprise application servers, software build pipelines, development environments, and moderate web application deployments requiring balanced CPU and memory resources.
